doc.title: Jimmy Lewis interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995

title: Why the Basie group worked: how Basie shaped the sound
summary: Lewis explains Basie chose compatible players and told them how to sound like Basie.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: The success of that group — what do you think it was attributed to? Just because you had such a great rhythm?

Well, Basie, see he knew how to select guys that would fit together. And then after he’d get the guys he’d talk to them. He’d say, “Look, this is what I want—this is the way I want you to sound.” He said, “You know to sound like Basie you have to play this way.” And he’d tell them what he’d want. And somebody would come and bring an arrangement, and he’d take the arrangement and listen to it. He’d say, “All right now, I want to take that section out of the trumpet there, that eight bar, and leave that open for me.” And he’d say “Now I want you to do this and I want you to use your hats in certain places, and your plungers, and the trumpets I want you to just shake the notes in certain place.” And then you’d say, “okay.” And we’d get up and we’d do it. He said, “Now that sounds like Basie.” Boy that was something.
This is great. I know you’ve got so much stuff.
I’ve got so much stuff that I haven’t even gotten to yet.
